text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT declared: hosted-api queue growth -> GPU pool autoscaler failing to provision. Paging oncall.

maya (oncall): seeing p95 go from 320ms -> 12s over last 6m, p99 ~45s. queue depth @ ~11.8k requests. dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dash/hosted/queue

maya (oncall): errors are timeouts and 504s surfaced to customers, support already triaging. tagging infra.

james (infra): looking. autoscaler logs show repeated attempts to create instances but failing with AWS error: "InsufficientInstanceCapacity: Not enough capacity in request region" and also occasional "RequestLimitExceeded" when retrying.

liz (infra): autoscaler logic seems to hit "maxPoolSize" cap for hosted-gpu pool for some accounts — config shows pool max=120, current active 118, scaler tried to add 8 but bounded. also some reserved nodes are unhealthy (2) so effective capacity lower.

maya (oncall): customers hitting timeouts include: prod-analytics (high qps), chat-widget-prod (heavy bursts). Support please gather request ids and any customer-facing errors.

ash (support): triage: we've got ~37 tickets started, 4 customers reporting intermittent request timeouts. Notified support-handoff. ETA for initial comms: 15m once we confirm root cause.

james (infra): temp mitigation plan: 1) increase pool max and bump reserved nodes 2) enable emergency fallback routing to smaller model variants (quantized) for non-LL-critical routes 3) open cloud quota requests asap. I'll try manual pool bump now.

liz (infra): agree. manual bump command run from infra-console:

```
# bump pool max & force-provision
redwoodctl pools update hosted-gpu --max-size 160
redwoodctl pools provision hosted-gpu --count 10 --reason "incident: capacity bump"
```

james (infra): ran provision command. cloud API returned mixed results: 6 nodes created, 4 failed with InsufficientInstanceCapacity. Provisioned GPUs available: +6. still short ~20 nodes to reach target throughput.

maya (oncall): enabling request-level mitigation: reduce model concurrency and enable prefix caching for high-cost routes. patching routing policy to allow fallbacks.

liz (infra): applied routing change: hosted-route -> allow-fallback: true for route tags chat-widget-prod, analytics-prod

maya (oncall): commands used to flip fallback:

```
redwoodctl routes update hosted-api --tag chat-widget-prod --fallback-enabled true
redwoodctl routes update hosted-api --tag analytics-prod --fallback-enabled true
```

anya (pm): for customer comms: what's impact window and estimated restoration? we need a short blurb for customers.

ash (support): initial blurb: "We're experiencing degraded API performance for some hosted endpoints due to capacity provisioning issues. We're actively remediate; some requests may time out or be slower. We'll update in 30 minutes or sooner." ok?

maya (oncall): fine. include suggestion: "If you see 504s, please retry after 5s, and contact support with request id." will post to status page. I'm drafting.

james (infra): further mitigation: temporarily lower default model size for low-tier plans to a 7B quantized variant to free up GPU slots. Doing rollout can be done via runtime config rollouts.

liz (infra): triggering rollout:

```
redwoodctl rollout create --target hosted-runtime --config '{"model_policy":{"default":"7b-quant-q4"}}' --canary 10%
```

james (infra): canary passed quickly, rolling to 50%. This reduces per-request token compute by ~40% based on benchmark, should reduce queue drain time.

maya (oncall): p95 trending down to ~2.1s after fallbacks and +6 nodes, queue depth -> 6.1k. still some tail timeouts but improving.

ash (support): posting update to customers and updating tickets.

anya (pm): thanks — we'll open an incident status on the public status page.

maya (oncall): additional note: autoscaler had a bug when cloud returns "InsufficientInstanceCapacity" + retry -> it toggles to exponential backoff and reduces desired capacity, which in combination with hitting maxPoolSize caused the stall. We'll mark as probable root cause for follow-up.

james (infra): created a short-term fix PR to stop reducing desired capacity on InsufficientInstanceCapacity errors; instead it should leave desired untouched and escalate to manual ops. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/autoscaler/pulls/4321

liz (infra): also scheduling a quota increase with cloud team; submitted request to provider support for target capacity in the region and a warm pool of 30 instances.

maya (oncall): handoff to infra for long-running remediations. I'll continue to monitor for 30m and then hand to SRE for postmortem.

sre-roster: acknowledged. tagging postmortem owners and oncall rotation. please snapshot logs and metrics for 18:30-19:15 UTC window.

maya (oncall): final update: queue down to 1.2k, p95 ~480ms, p99 ~3.2s. customer impact reduced. keeping incident open for follow-through. posting incident summary shortly.

ash (support): support comms posted. customers with high-severity tickets are being handled via direct emails.

anya (pm): follow-ups: 1) autoscaler robustness fix 2) region warm pools 3) improve fallback policies per-customer 4) runbook update for handoffs. scheduling follow-up meeting.

maya (oncall): closing live mitigation. incident status -> monitoring. If anything regresses, escalate back to oncall immediately. :thumbsup:
